writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: content:check run for the batch and writer; no errors or warnings on this item. Claims: every checkable statement is listed, distractors included; c3 (superlative), c4 (number) and c5 (number) are high under the C26 floor, and c1 and c2 are standard. Datasets: natural-earth ne_50m_lakes holds Lake Baikal as a polygon in southern Siberia, north of the Mongolian border (c1, c2). No dataset gives depth or volume. Rival test: Mongolia is the pull, because the lake lies close to its northern border; Kazakhstan and China are big neighbours with famous lakes of their own. Against the key: nothing; the lake lies wholly in Russia. Volatility: evergreen, settled geography with no review date; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: Baikal is world-famous as the deepest lake, and the stem's 'deepest' claim is undisputed. Style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, straight apostrophes, explanation of 22 words. Myths: every claim screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. Mystery and encore: nothing of either kind to check in a practice item. External evidence: c3, c4 and c5 need a web result (one search should cover the depth and the share of fresh water). Seed: 2 (easy): most players know Baikal is in Siberia. Counterintuitive: false. Doubts: the share of fresh water is quoted between about 20% and 23%, so c5 says 'about a fifth'; the depth is about 1,640 m, so c4 uses a safe bound.
